newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece wants EU, IMF to aid troubled Balkan states.
newsitem.headline: Greece wants EU, IMF to aid troubled Balkan states.

text.p: Greece said on Tuesday it would propose that the European Union should give ecomomic backing to Balkan countries such as Albania and Bulgaria in a bid to restore stability to the region.

"Greece will make a proposal at the EU's general affairs council on February 24 to financially support Balkan countries such as Albania and Bulgaria," foreign ministry spokesman Costas Bikas told Reuters.
The plan would call for support from a list of organisations apart from the EU, such as the International Monetary Fund, the European Investment Bank and other investors.
"We are interested in stability in the Balkans and Europe," Bikas said. "We have already briefed the ambassadors of fellow member states about this new Greek initiative."
Greece, the only Balkan country to belong to the EU, has been swamped by hundreds of thousands of illegal refugees from the Balkans after the fall of communism in 1989 and 1990.
Greek officials said they were concerned a fresh wave of immigrants would descend on its already taxed economy because of recent upheavals in Bulgaria and Albania.
Unrest in Albania over the collapse of pyramid investment schemes has claimed lives in clashes between Albanians left destitute and police.
Bulgaria, also deep in financial crisis, has also faced a wave of heated protests in recent weeks.
